groups.notes: Ten eligible units; all started at ladder index 0, the only starting step this repository has measured. Recommendation retained at claude:claude-sonnet-5/low with low confidence because evidence remains single-armed. Three units were accepted without a material fix/re-review; seven required one or more. #111 is correctly counted as material re-review: one Standards finding, one Spec finding, and two fix passes (unit fix plus root test-evidence remediation). Its implementation started and finished at Sonnet 5/low. Two planner API-529 failures, one reviewer sandbox failure, the nested-PTY row, and the root-remediation Codex attempts all carry capabilityFailure:false or are environment/integration evidence, so none support a route floor increase. #111 reports null usage, cost, token, and duration values; it is included in sample counts but excluded from dollar medians, which retain nine cost-reporting units. No capability failure exists and no comparable unit started at a stronger step, so neither the two-unit capability ground nor a 25%-cheaper stronger-step comparison can be established. Index 0 cannot be lowered and no lower boundary probe exists. Cost remains confounded by change/context size and attempt count; do not compare this median across groups without normalization.

groups.notes:
Five eligible units (#50, #57, #58, #112, #113); every one started at ladder index 0, still the only starting step this repository has ever measured for this group. Recommendation RETAINED unchanged at claude:claude-sonnet-5/low (index 0), confidence low.

#112 merged this run as a material re-review, not a clean success and not a capability escalation. Its implementer started at index 0 (Sonnet 5/low, outcome retry, capabilityFailure:false) and completed at index 1 (Sonnet 5/medium, purpose recovery, capabilityFailure:false) with review.fixPasses=1. escalations[0] is dimension=effort, raised under the material-non-clean-fix-pass rule in model-routing.md. Per the rubric that is an effort raise on a non-clean review, NOT a model-capability failure, so it increments materialReReview and leaves capabilityEscalation at 0 and observedBoundary.highestCapabilityFailure at null.

Boundary rubric applied at n=5, no change permitted in either direction. Raise ground (a) requires >=2 units needing the same or a stronger step for CAPABILITY reasons: this group has zero such units, every attempt across all five carries capabilityFailure:false. Raise ground (b) requires >=2 units showing a stronger step materially cheaper to acceptance (>=25% lower median costToAcceptance): no unit in this group has ever STARTED above index 0, so there is no stronger-step arm to compare against and the comparison cannot be computed. #112's index-1 finish is an observed successful recovery step, not a measured index-1 starting cost, so it is deliberately not added as a costToAcceptance arm. Lowering is impossible because index 0 is the lowest verified step in the claude ladder; for the same reason boundaryProbe.due stays false, as there is nothing below index 0 to probe. Net ladder steps changed this run: zero.

Data-quality caveats that hold confidence at low. (1) Evidence is single-armed: one starting step, no contrast. (2) #50, #57 and #58 are LEGACY pre-schema-2 records carrying costUsd/turns/durationMin but no route, model or effort field. Per the calibrate rubric, legacy records count only as model-level evidence and their unknown effort must never be backfilled or used to infer an effort boundary; only #112 and #113 have verified route-and-effort attribution at index 0. byStep.units=5 therefore counts units observed at this step, while medianTotal 13.09 USD still rests on the three legacy cost-reporting units only (#57 9.28, #58 13.09, #50 17.75, per-unit sums across attempts). (3) #112 and #113 both report null token, credit, cost and currency values because the harnesses expose no usage data on the claude.ai subscription; both are counted in samples and excluded from the dollar median. #112 does report durationMs, so durationMsRange extends to 2504000 ms on the same per-unit convention as the legacy rows (implementer attempts plus merger: 992000 + 890000 + 622000). Planner and reviewer attempts are excluded from that sum to stay comparable with the legacy rows, and reviewer routing is never an input to implementer calibration. (4) Cost remains confounded by change and context size; do not compare this median across groups without normalization.
